content:
In France, the national social security system fully covers prenatal and postnatal medical care in public hospitals. Women in paid employment are granted 16 weeks of maternity leave, during which they receive daily compensation ranging from €9.29 ($10.94) to €84.90 ($100), depending on their previous earnings. 

Financially, pregnancy and the period around birth do not bring extra strain compared with other times: families already facing hardship continue to do so, and more prosperous families remain comfortable. In terms of practical and emotional support for new mothers, though, there is effectively no structured help in place. 

Partners are allowed just 11 days of leave, which is insufficient even for the mother to physically recover from giving birth. New mothers are left to cope with constant daily responsibilities while still healing. They must also find childcare, despite the fact that public options are lacking, particularly in the Paris area. Costs vary widely. In public crèches, the least well-off families may pay about €1,000 ($1,177.59) per year, but there is only one available spot for every eight children. As a result, many families turn to private solutions such as childminders or in-home caregivers. Any other questions?
